'''Takehiratori no Mikoto''' ({{lang|ja|建比良鳥命}}) is a {{ill|Kami|ja|神 (神道)|lt=god|lt_ja=神}} who appears in {{ill|Japanese mythology|ja|日本神話|lt=Japanese mythology|lt_ja=日本神話}}.

== Overview ==
The god is written '''Takehiratori no Mikoto''' in the ''Kojiki''; '''Ōsobi no Mikuma no Ushi''' (大背飯三熊之大人), '''Takemikuma no Ushi''' (武三熊之大人), '''Takehinateru''' (武日照命), '''Takehinatori''' (武夷鳥) and '''Ame-no-Hinatori''' (天夷鳥) in the ''Nihon Shoki''; and '''Ame-no-Hinatori no Mikoto''' (天夷鳥命) and '''Ame-no-Hinadori no Mikoto''' (天日名鳥命) in the ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録|lt=Shinsen Shōjiroku|lt_ja=新撰姓氏録}}''. The identification of these alternative names rests on the ''Izumo-no-kuni no Miyatsuko Dentō Ryaku'', a genealogy handed down by the {{ill|Senge family|ja|出雲国造#千家家|lt=Senge family|lt_ja=千家家}}, who as the house of the Izumo ''kuni no miyatsuko'' inherited the rites of {{ill|Izumo-taisha|ja|出雲大社|lt=Izumo-taisha|lt_ja=出雲大社}}.{{Sfn|千家|1882}}

In the name, ''take'' means "brave", and ''hira'' shares its origin with ''heri'' ("edge"), meaning the end of a thing or the border with the next; the name is taken to mean "the brave bird that flies across the border to another land". The ''hira'' of {{ill|Yomotsu Hirasaka|ja|黄泉比良坂|lt=Yomotsu Hirasaka|lt_ja=黄泉比良坂}} likewise means the border between {{ill|Yomi|ja|黄泉国|lt=Yomi|lt_ja=黄泉国}} and the {{ill|This world|ja|現世|lt=land of the living|lt_ja=現し国}}; the ''hera'' of the Herazaka slope in Yamashiro is a village boundary, and the ''bera'' of {{ill|Okitsukaibera|ja|奥津甲斐弁羅神|lt=Okitsukaibera no Kami|lt_ja=奥津甲斐弁羅神}} is the boundary between sea and land. As with {{ill|Torimimi|ja|鳥取神|lt=Torimimi no Kami|lt_ja=鳥取神}}, {{ill|Torinarumi|ja|鳥鳴海神|lt=Torinarumi no Kami|lt_ja=鳥鳴海神}} and {{ill|Nunooshitomitorinarumi|ja|布忍富鳥鳴海神|lt=Nunooshitomitorinarumi no Kami|lt_ja=布忍富鳥鳴海神}}, the name reflects the belief that birds carry human souls to another land, and the "border to another land" is thought to be the border of {{ill|Izumo Province|ja|出雲国|lt=Izumo Province|lt_ja=出雲国}}.{{Sfn|西宮|2014|pp=364-365}}

The alternative name Ame-no-Hinatori no Mikoto means "the bird that flew down from {{ill|Takamagahara|ja|高天原|lt=Takamagahara|lt_ja=高天原}} to the ''hina'' (the countryside, that is, Izumo)", so it is taken to be the same divine figure as Takehiratori.{{Sfn|西宮|2014|pp=364-365}}

== Accounts ==
In the ''Kojiki'', in the episode of {{ill|Ukehi|ja|アマテラスとスサノオの誓約|lt=the oath of Amaterasu and Susanoo|lt_ja=天照大御神と須佐之男命の誓約}}, Takehiratori is the son of {{ill|Ame-no-Hohi|ja|アメノホヒ|lt=Ame-no-Hohi|lt_ja=天之菩卑能命}} and the ancestral god of the Izumo, Musashi, Kamitsuunakami, Shimotsuunakami and Ijimu ''kuni no miyatsuko'', the Tsushima ''agata no atai'', the Tōtōmi ''kuni no miyatsuko'' and others.
{{Quotation|天菩比命之子、建比良鳥命 【此出雲國造无耶志國造上菟上國造下菟上國造伊自牟國造津嶋縣直遠江國造等之祖也】<br>"The son of Ame-no-Hohi was Takehiratori no Mikoto. (He is the ancestor of the Izumo kuni no miyatsuko, the Musashi kuni no miyatsuko, the Kamitsuunakami kuni no miyatsuko, the Shimotsuunakami kuni no miyatsuko, the Ijimu kuni no miyatsuko, the Tsushima agata no atai, the Tōtōmi kuni no miyatsuko and others.)"|''Kojiki''}}
In the ''Nihon Shoki'', in the pacification of {{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|ja|葦原中国|lt=Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|lt_ja=葦原中国}}, Ōsobi no Mikuma no Ushi (also called Takemikuma no Ushi) was sent to Ashihara no Nakatsukuni after his father Ame-no-Hohi, but like his father he sent back no report. The ''Nihon Shoki'' also records that in the seventh month of the 60th year of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇|lt=Emperor Sujin|lt_ja=崇神天皇}}, the emperor said he wished to see the {{ill|Shinpō|ja|神宝|lt=sacred treasures|lt_ja=神宝}} that Takehinateru (also called Takehinatori or Ame-no-Hinatori) had brought from heaven, which were kept at the great shrine of Izumo, and had them presented; this led to strife within the Izumo clan, and its head at the time, {{ill|Izumo Furune|ja|出雲振根|lt=Izumo Furune|lt_ja=出雲振根}}, was put to death.

The ''{{ill|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|ja|日本文徳天皇実録|lt=Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|lt_ja=日本文徳天皇実録}}'', under the 22nd day of the third month of {{ill|Ten'an (Japanese era)|ja|天安 (日本)|lt=Ten'an|lt_ja=天安}} 2 (858), records "Ame-no-Hinatori no Mikoto in Kawachi Province is granted Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade", taken to mean the Ame-no-Hinatori enshrined at today's {{ill|Dōmyōji Tenmangū|ja|道明寺天満宮|lt=Dōmyōji Tenmangū|lt_ja=道明寺天満宮}}.
{{Quotation|{{collapse top|Original text}}天照太神之子。正哉吾勝勝速日天忍穗耳尊。娶高皇產靈尊之女栲幡千千姫。生天津火瓊瓊杵尊。故皇祖高皇產靈尊。特鍾憐愛以崇養焉。遂欲立皇孫天津火瓊瓊杵尊以爲葦原中國之主。然彼地多有螢火光神及蝿聲邪神。復有草木咸能言語。故高皇產靈尊召集八十諸神。而問之曰。吾欲令撥平葦原中國之邪鬼。當遣誰者宜也。惟爾諸神勿隱所知。僉曰。天穗日命是神之傑也。可不試歟。於是、俯順衆言。即以天穗日命往平之。然此神侫媚於大己貴神。比及三年尚不報聞。故仍遣其子大背飯三熊之大人。〈大人。此云于志。〉亦名武三熊之大人。此亦還順其父。遂不報聞。{{collapse bottom}}
In summary: Takamimusubi wished to make his grandson Ninigi lord of Ashihara no Nakatsukuni, but the land was full of gods that shone like fireflies, evil gods that buzzed like flies, and plants and trees that could speak. He called the eighty gods together and asked whom to send to subdue its evil spirits; all said Ame-no-Hohi was the finest of the gods. Ame-no-Hohi was sent, but he curried favour with Ōnamuchi and for three years sent no report. So his son Ōsobi no Mikuma no Ushi, also called Takemikuma no Ushi, was sent, but he too followed his father and never reported back.|''Nihon Shoki'', book 2, "Age of the Gods, part 2"}}
{{Quotation|{{collapse top|Original text}}《崇神天皇六〇年（癸未前三八）七月己酉（十四）》六十年秋七月丙申朔己酉。詔群臣曰。武日照命。〈　一云。武夷鳥。又云。天夷鳥。　〉従天将来神宝。蔵于出雲大神宮。是欲見焉。則遣矢田部造遠祖武諸隅、〈　一書云。一名大母隅也。　〉而使献。当是時。出雲臣之遠祖出雲振根主于神宝。是往筑紫国而不遇矣。其弟飯入根則被皇命。以神宝、付弟甘美韓日狭与子鸕濡渟而貢上。既而出雲振根従筑紫還来之。聞神宝献于朝廷。責其弟飯入根曰。数日当待。何恐之乎。輒許神宝。是以既経年月。猶懐恨忿、有殺弟之志。仍欺弟曰。頃者於止屋淵多生菨。願共行欲見。則随兄而往之。先是。兄窃作木刀。形似真刀。当時自佩之。弟佩真刀。共到淵頭。兄謂弟曰。淵水清冷。願欲共游沐。弟従兄言。各解佩刀、置淵辺。沐於水中。乃兄先上陸。取弟真刀自佩。後弟驚而取兄木刀。共相撃矣。弟不得抜木刀。兄撃弟飯入根而殺之。故時人歌之曰。椰句毛多菟　伊頭毛多鶏流餓　波鶏流多知　菟頭邏佐波磨枳　佐微那辞珥　阿波礼{{efn|''Yakumo tatsu / Izumo takeru ga / hakeru tachi / tsuzura sawa maki / sami nashi ni / aware'' (Nihon Shoki poem 20).}} 於是甘美韓日狭。鸕濡渟。参向朝廷、曲奏其状。則遣吉備津彦与武渟河別。以誅出雲振根。故出雲臣等畏是事。不祭大神而有間。時丹波氷上人。名氷香戸辺。啓于皇太子活目尊曰。己子有小児。而自然言之。玉菨鎮石。出雲人祭。真種之甘美鏡。押羽振。甘美御神、底宝御宝主。山河之水泳御魂。静挂甘美御神、底宝御宝主也。〈　菨。此云毛。　〉是非似小児之言。若有託言乎。於是。皇太子奏于天皇。則勅之使祭。{{collapse bottom}}
In summary: in the seventh month of Sujin 60, the emperor told his ministers he wished to see the sacred treasures that Takehinateru (also called Takehinatori or Ame-no-Hinatori) had brought from heaven and that were kept at the great shrine of Izumo, and sent Takemorosumi, ancestor of the Yatabe no miyatsuko, to have them presented. Izumo Furune, who had charge of the treasures, was away in Tsukushi, so his younger brother Iiirine obeyed the command and had them sent up. When Furune returned and heard this, he resented his brother and resolved to kill him. He invited him to bathe at the Yamuya pool, having secretly carved a wooden sword that looked like a real one; when both had left their swords on the bank and gone into the water, Furune came out first, took his brother's real sword, and killed him when the brother could not draw the wooden one. People of the time sang of it. When Umashikarahisa and Ukazukunu reported this to the court, Kibitsuhiko and Takenunakawawake were sent to execute Furune, and for a time the Izumo clan, in fear, did not worship the great god. Then a child in Tanba began to speak words like an oracle about the worship of the god of Izumo; the crown prince reported this to the emperor, who ordered the worship resumed.|''Nihon Shoki'', book 5, "Sujin"}}
In book 8 of the ''Engishiki'', the {{ill|Izumo-no-kuni no miyatsuko kamuyogoto|ja|出雲国造神賀詞|lt=Izumo-no-kuni no miyatsuko kamuyogoto|lt_ja=出雲国造神賀詞}} contains the passage "[Ame-no-Hohi] sent down Ame-no-Hinatori no Mikoto, accompanied by {{ill|Futsunushi|ja|経津主神|lt=Futsunushi no Mikoto|lt_ja=布都怒志命}}".

== Genealogy ==
According to the ''Kojiki'', the ''Nihon Shoki'' and other works, Takehiratori is the son of Ame-no-Hohi, one of the five sons of {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|lt=Amaterasu|lt_ja=天照大御神}}. The genealogy of the Izumo ''kuni no miyatsuko'' makes the next generation Isaga no Mikoto (Kushini no Mikoto).{{Sfn|千家|1882}}
